claims.text: The PATTERN:ex libris signal (candidate c-20261007-05) is generated from exactly one TED notice, 690422-2026 — a single lot, single framework-agreement award, single winner ("EX LIBRIS") shared by 12 co-contracting EU-institution buyers across 5 countries (BEL, DEU, LUX, MLT, PRT) — not from five separate, independently decided contract awards.

Notice 690422-2026 (contract award notice, published 2026-10-07) is the award-stage publication of a procedure for which a contract notice (57057-2026) with the identical 12-buyer set, identical CPV code 72212160 and identical multilingual title was already public on 2026-01-26, more than 8 months earlier.

The sole occurrence of the envelope phrase 'artificial intelligence' in notice 690422-2026, the reason the notice entered the observatory's AI-procurement envelope, is inside the postal address of the contracting buyer's contact department name ("OP.A ... and Artificial Intelligence Exploitation"), not in any description of the procured Library Services Platform.

Across TED's current index, only 3 contract-award notices combine winner-name 'ex libris' with CPV 72212160 (library software development services): one single-buyer-country award each in Italy (2024) and the Netherlands (2025), and this one 5-country joint award (2026). No other independent multi-country 'ex libris' award exists in TED alongside 690422-2026.
